parts.answer: Resultant $=33.6\,\mathrm{N}$, directed $64.8^\circ$ above the $14\,\mathrm{N}$ force (equivalently $25.2^\circ$ above the negative $x$-axis, $25.2^\circ$ left of the $60\,\mathrm{N}$ force, bearing $335^\circ$, or $115^\circ$ anticlockwise from the positive $x$-axis).
parts.official_mark_scheme_text:
Resolve in either direction. — M1: three terms; allow sign errors and sine/cosine mix.
$X=\pm(20\cos60^\circ-14-16\cos50^\circ)=\pm14.2846\ldots$. — A1.
$Y=\pm(60-20\sin60^\circ-16\sin50^\circ)=\pm30.42278\ldots$. — A1.
$R=\sqrt{14.2846^2+30.42278^2}$. — M1: attempt to solve for $R$; one missing term in total.
$\theta=\tan^{-1}(30.42278/14.2846)$ or $\alpha=\tan^{-1}(14.2846/30.42278)$. — M1: attempt to solve for $\theta$ or $\alpha$; one missing term in total.
$R=33.6\,\mathrm{N}$. Direction is $64.8^\circ$ above the $14\,\mathrm{N}$ force, or $25.2^\circ$ above the negative $x$-axis, or $25.2^\circ$ left of the $60\,\mathrm{N}$ force, or bearing $335^\circ$, or $115^\circ$ anticlockwise from the positive $x$-axis. — A1 for both correct; allow $64.9^\circ$ or $25.1^\circ$.
Giving an angle only is insufficient. Direction may be shown on a diagram with at least an arrow on the resultant. Arrows on both components only are A0 because they do not show the resultant direction. However stated, the direction must be uniquely drawable.
Total: 6.
